introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah says that if we share our bread with the hungry, our light will break forth like the dawn. In the Gospel, Jesus tells his disciples, You are the salt of the earth; you are the light of the world. Paul tells the Corinthians that he came to them knowing nothing but Jesus Christ crucified. Let our light shine before others, so that they may see our good works and give glory to God.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ is the light of the world, and he calls us to be light. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be salt and light in the world through her works of mercy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the hungry, the homeless and those without clothing: that Christians may share with them generously. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live in darkness and despair: that our good works may bring them light and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For preachers and teachers: that they may proclaim Christ crucified, trusting in the power of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that our light may shine so that others give glory to our Father in heaven. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son is the light of the world. Let our lives shine with his light through works of justice and mercy, so that all may give you glory. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Salt and light
reflection.body:
Isaiah tells the people what kind of religion pleases God. It is not only fasting and prayer, but "to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house." When we do this, he says, "your light will break out as the morning, and your healing will appear quickly." And God will answer our prayers: "You will cry for help, and he will say," Here I am. Light comes from love.

In the Gospel, right after the Beatitudes, Jesus tells his disciples who they are. He does not say "try to become" salt and light. He says, "You are the salt of the earth... You are the light of the world." This is our identity as Christians.

Salt gives flavor and preserves food from decay. Christians are meant to bring flavor and goodness to the world and to resist what corrupts it. But Jesus warns that salt can lose its taste, and then it is useless. Light is meant to be seen: "A city located on a hill can't be hidden. Neither do you light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket." Faith that is kept entirely private is like a lamp under a basket.

Then Jesus tells us the purpose of our light: "let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven." The goal is not our own glory but God's.

Paul shows the humility this requires. He did not come to Corinth with clever words: "For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified." The power was God's, not his.

This week, let your light shine in one concrete way: share food with someone hungry, visit someone alone, or speak a word of truth with kindness. Do it for God's glory, not your own.
